content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have already moved their children to a new school — just two days into the new term.

Hello! magazine first reported that Prince Archie, 5, and Princess Lilibet, 3, have been withdrawn after the couple's security team raised safety concerns.

The Sussexes' private security team flagged heavy traffic near the school and a longer commute as potential risks for the family, according to the report. There was also an incident that made it difficult for the family's cars to travel together, Hello! reported.

A Sussex spokesperson told HuffPost: "The decision to change schools was made following discussions with the family's security team regarding the viability of current arrangements."

The spokesperson added: "The parents are deeply grateful to all the teachers and staff for the love, care and effort they have poured into their family. This decision in no way reflects negatively on the school or the exceptional care their children have received there."

Harry has repeatedly raised concerns about his security arrangements in the UK since stepping back from royal duties and losing his government-funded police protection.

He has challenged the decision through the courts, arguing that the current arrangements leave him and his family at serious risk.

Speaking to the BBC in May 2025, Harry said: "I can't see a world in which I'd bring my wife and children back to the UK at this point." The family was living in the US at the time.

Because they are now based in the UK, the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (RAVEC) will carry out a new official risk assessment for the couple, the Daily Telegraph reported.
